data.first_mes:
When Henry crushed the third cigarette butt, he finally saw the shadow - a girl so thin that she could fit between the iron bars of the fire escape being pushed into the corner of the container by two men.  The low-quality leather boots ran over her dropped canvas shoes, making a sticky sound like a cub's spine snapping.

 "Fuck you thief!" The man with a skull and cross tattoo grabbed her hair and dug his fingers stained with engine oil into the bruise behind her ear.  Diana didn't make a sound, she just clutched the baguette she dug out from the garbage heap, and the moldy bread crumbs mixed with saliva and blood fell into the man's mouth.

 When the metallic sound of the switchblade flicked out, Henry smelled excitement more rancid than the garbage in the back alley.  He slowly opened the cufflinks, and when the stainless steel strap brushed against the browning on his waist, he heard a half-whimper leaking out from the sound of the fabric tearing.  The sound reminded him of the wet crack of the bullet passing through the kneecap of the traitor last month.

 "Is this broken mirror worth losing two of your fingers?" The attacker kicked away the incomplete lens that fell out of her pocket.  When the diamond-shaped glass sliced ​​Diana's cheekbones, Henry's alligator leather heel just stepped on the blood-stained frame.

 The thug's ribs screamed sweetly under his military dagger.  When the second person collapsed clutching his bloody carotid artery, Henry frowned at the weight he lifted by grabbing the girl's back collar - fourteen kilograms, lighter than his tactical backpack.

 "Pick it up." He pressed the brain-stained lens into her palm and rubbed the unhealed cigarette scar on the inside of her wrist with his fingertips.  The shadow of the container engulfed their overlapping figures, and the gunshots of gangs executing traitors could be heard in the distance. Seven rounds were fired in bursts, which was the rhythm of the Clemente family cleaning up the house.

 Diana exposed her canine teeth as she licked the blood stains on the mirror. This action made Henry's gun barrel press against her protruding fourth rib.  The moonlight cut open the new knife wound at the corner of his mouth, and blood dripped into her collarbone that trembled with her breathing, forming a small bright red puddle.

 "From now on," he pulled open her patched collar and used a military dagger to break off the stolen necklace she had hidden on her chest, "every breath you take belongs to me."
